title: Activation conductor: shift rotation & steward playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic playbook for steward rotation across canary / A/B exposures. Focus: reduce steward fatigue, ensure continuous signal coverage across timezones, and make handoffs low-friction so experiments can run 24/7 without signal gaps. WIP — meant to be lightweight and testable in next sprint.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Steward role definitions (primary, secondary, relief) for canaries and AB cohorts.
- A recommended rotation algorithm + overlap policy.
- Handoff checklist and Slack templates.
- Fatigue scoring heuristic and simulation plan.
- Escalation ladder and minimal pager protocol (no noisy alerts).
- Runbook for shift reassignments during holidays/coverage gaps.

Quick notes to self / constraints: 
- We try to avoid adding extra oncall headcount; prefer rotation among existing stewards in product/observability/engineering.
- Canary exposures can be short (minutes) or long (days). Rotation model must support both.
- We want at least 2 humans (primary + secondary) during high-risk activations; single steward OK for low-risk microcanaries.

Role definitions (working):
- Primary steward: owns the experiment slice for the active shift window. Responsible for triage, comms, and quick rollback decisions.
- Secondary steward: watches signals, ready to take over in 15m, acts as backup and author of post-incident notes.
- Relief / rotation partner: picks up the next shift and shadow-hands off.
- Owner (experiment lead): not necessarily on every shift — accountable for hypothesis, metrics, and final decisions.

Recommended cadence / rotation algorithm (proposal):
- Shifts are 8 hours in UTC-aligned blocks: 00-08, 08-16, 16-00. Simpler for global teams and overlap planning.
- Rotation window = 3 shifts per steward (i.e., steward covers 24 hours across 3 sequential shifts) for high-touch canaries, then rotates out for at least 48 hours off steward duty (cooldown).
- For low-touch microcanaries, steward covers 1 shift then rotates.
- Overlap policy: 30 minute overlap between outgoing and incoming primary during handoff; 15 minute overlap for secondary if available.

Rationale: 8-hour blocks minimize waking people in the middle of night repeatedly and keeps cognitive load predictable. The 24-on / 48-off pattern reduces fatigue for high-risk experiments but is heavier on staffing; simulation below helps decide tradeoffs.

Fatigue scoring heuristic (for staffing simulations):
- Score per steward per day = 2 * (number of high-risk shift-hours) + 1 * (low-risk shift-hours) + 3 * (number of interrupts outside shift) + 2 * (number of handoffs in 24h)
- If score > 18 over sliding 7-day window -> auto-enforce additional cooldown (assign alternate).
- Track interrupts via Slack channel tagging + incident log.

Handoff checklist (outgoing -> incoming):
- State summary: hypothesis, expected user-visible change, slice description (cohort ids), duration target.
- Telemetry pointer: one-line links to the dashboard(s) + synthetic checks.
- Current signal health snapshot (latency, error rate, quality delta if available).
- Any ongoing mitigations or partial rollbacks.
- Escalation contacts: SRE oncall, model-owner, product lead, legal (if PII risk).
- Confirmation: incoming acknowledges readiness in Slack and marks timestamp.
- If any critical signals present, keep both primary+secondary for an extra shift.

Minimal pager policy (to avoid alarm fatigue):
- Pager is reserved for: safety breach (exposed PII), latency violation exceeding X ms sustained for 5m, error rate > 3x baseline sustained for 10m, model output safety signals above threshold.
- All other signal degradation should be routed to Slack experiment-channel with @steward mention and a severity tag.

Slack templates (copy/paste):
- Handoff start (outgoing):
  "Handoff START: @incoming @secondary — experiment: [exp-id]. Hypothesis: [short]. Current health: latency 140ms (+10), error-rate 0.8% (ok). Dash: <link>. Notes: throttled to 10% by router. Out at 12:30 UTC (30m overlap)."
- Handoff complete (incoming):
  "Handoff COMPLETE: @outgoing -> @incoming. Accepting stewardship for [exp-id]. Confirmed dashboards ok. Will escalate to SRE if latency > 200ms for 10m."

Simulation plan (to validate staffing tradeoffs):
- Inputs: number of active experiments, risk classification (low/med/high), expected interrupt frequency (from historical logs), timezone distribution of stewards.
- Sim: run 28-day randomized schedule generator using rotation rules. Compute fatigue scores, overlap gaps, and coverage holes.
- Success criteria: no coverage hole > 60 minutes for any high-risk experiment; median fatigue score < 12; <5 emergency escalations per 30-day window in simulated history.

Sample rotation pseudocode (high-level):
- steward_list = ordered list by timezone coverage and domain expertise
- for each high_risk_experiment:
    assign consecutive_shifts = 3 // configurable
    assign primary = steward_list.pop_front()
    reserve secondary = steward_list.peek(0)
    mark primary.calendar(blocks=consecutive_shifts)
    after consecutive_shifts: push primary to cooldown_queue (48h)
- If cooldown_queue empty and no steward available -> auto-scale: mark experiment read-only throttle to 5% and notify owner.

Runbook: immediate actions for primary steward on signal degradation
1) Confirm signal (dashboard + synthetic test).
2) Reduce exposure slice to safe baseline (e.g., 0% or graceful degrade to baseline model).
3) Notify experiment-channel with short post and tag owner + SRE.
4) Open triage ticket with snapshot and attach logs.
5) If rollback executed, run mini-retro and update canary ticket within 24h.

Edge cases and holiday coverage:
- Public holiday overlap: prefer volunteers and explicitly rotate shorter shifts (4-hour handover windows) to increase flexibility.
- Single-steward coverage allowed only for low-risk slices; require explicit owner sign-off.
- If steward becomes unreachable during overlap: secondary takes primary role immediately, and emergency owner is paged.

Measurement & dashboards to build (owner suggestions):
- Steward coverage heatmap (who covered which experiment by shift).
- Fatigue dashboard (weekly score per steward).
- Shift handoff latency (time between outgoing COMPLETE and incoming ACCEPT).
- Incidents per steward per experiment (normalized).

Open questions / items to decide: (quick list for review)
- Exact numeric thresholds for fatigue cooldown — start with heuristic above, tune with sim.
- Do we prefer fixed 8h blocks in all regions or allow local TZ splits for large regional teams?
- Is 24-on / 48-off sustainable with our current headcount? Run sim and present to EMs.
- Which Slack channel will be canonical for handoff transcripts? (proposal: #canary-orchestra)

Next steps (short):
- [Ethan] run baseline sim this sprint and produce scoreboard (due 2025-02-21).
- [Priya] prototype the Steward coverage heatmap in Console (simple export view) — spike due 2025-02-28.
- [Maya] draft a short policy doc for minimal pager thresholds and share with SRE for buy-in (due 2025-02-18).

Notes / random scribbles: 
- Could include a light-weight bot to auto-post handoff reminders 10m before overlap end. Avoid over-automation initially.
- Consider a 4-week steward rotation pilot limited to experiments classified as high-value only.
- Document should live as a mutable Drive doc; after 2 pilot cycles convert to canonical Confluence page and add as linked artifact.

Appendix: quick risk taxonomy (for triage)
- Tier 1 (safety/legal): PII exfiltration, compliance breaches, regulatory-impacting outputs. Pager immediate.
- Tier 2 (availability): Latency and error spikes affecting user experience (>2x baseline for N minutes). Slack + SRE triage.
- Tier 3 (quality drift): Model outputs show measurable drop in quality / UX metric; owner + product to decide.

End of draft.

TODOs (in-doc):

- Draft Slack channel naming standards and add to linked_artifacts.
